def test_inconclusive_observation_rejects_closure(monkeypatch):
    def boom(sb, a):
        raise RuntimeError("observer unavailable")
    monkeypatch.setitem(verification.OBSERVERS, "dependent_healthy", boom)
    st, sb, e = mk()
    iid, rep = go(e)
    assert rep["status"] != "closed_verified"
    assert any(c["result"] is None for c in rep["conditions"])


def test_missing_conditions_reject_closure():
    st, sb, e = mk()
    iid, rep = go(e)
    st._x("DELETE FROM conditions WHERE incident_id=?", (iid,))
    rep2 = e.report(iid, live=True)
    assert rep2["status"] != "closed_verified" and not rep2["invariants"]["closure_conditions_defined"]


# 12. audit report matches actual actions and outcomes
def test_audit_report_matches_actions():
    st, sb, e = mk(scenario="signature")
    iid, rep = go(e)
    db = {a.id: a.status.value for a in st.actions(iid)}
    assert {a["id"]: a["status"] for a in rep["actions"]} == db
    evs = st.audit_events(iid)
    verified = {x["data"].get("action") for x in evs if x["event"] in ("verification_verified", "reconciled_verified")}
    assert {k for k, v in db.items() if v == "verified"} <= verified
    executed = [x["data"]["action"] for x in evs if x["event"] == "executing"]
    assert len(executed) == len(st.tool_calls(iid)) == rep["metrics"]["tool_calls"]
    assert st.incident(iid).status == rep["status"]
    assert len(st.approvals(iid)) == 1 and st.approvals(iid)[0]["by"] == "u-approver"
    with pytest.raises(Exception):
        st._x("DELETE FROM audit")
    with pytest.raises(Exception):
        st._x("UPDATE audit SET event='x'")


# 13. secret values are absent from storage, reports and traces
def test_secrets_absent_everywhere(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("ROOK_TRACE", "1")
    monkeypatch.setenv("ROOK_TRACE_DIR", str(tmp_path))
    assert "sk_test_SYNTH" not in redact({"k": "x sk_test_SYNTH_cred-pay_v2 y"})
    st, sb, e = mk(scenario="signature")
    iid, rep = go(e)
    blob = json.dumps([st.audit_events(iid), st.checkpoints(iid), st.tool_calls(iid), st.approvals(iid), rep,
                       st.incident(iid).model_dump(), [a.model_dump() for a in st.actions(iid)]], default=str)
    assert "sk_test_SYNTH" not in blob
    assert "sk_test_SYNTH" not in (tmp_path / "rook-trace.jsonl").read_text()

import json
import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from rook.api import DEMO_TOKENS, create_app

ANALYST, APPROVER, VIEWER, OTHER = ("demo-analyst-token", "demo-approver-token",
                                    "demo-viewer-token", "demo-other-org-token")


def h(token):
    return {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}

\[email]
def client(tmp_path):
    app = create_app(db_path=str(tmp_path / "api.db"), tokens=DEMO_TOKENS, step_delay=0, background=False)
    with TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False) as c:
        yield c


def new_incident(client, scenario="signature", token=ANALYST):
    r = client.post("/api/incidents", json={"scenario": scenario}, headers=h(token))
    assert r.status_code == 201, r.text
    return r.json()["id"]


def revoke_id(client, iid, token=ANALYST):
    rep = client.get(f"/api/incidents/{iid}", headers=h(token)).json()["report"]
    return next(a["id"] for a in rep["actions"] if a["type"] == "revoke_credential")


def test_full_flow_over_http(client):
    iid = new_incident(client)
    assert client.post(f"/api/incidents/{iid}/run", headers=h(ANALYST)).status_code == 202
    body = client.get(f"/api/incidents/{iid}", headers=h(ANALYST)).json()
    assert body["report"]["status"] == "awaiting_approval"
    r = client.post(f"/api/incidents/{iid}/actions/{revoke_id(client, iid)}/approve", headers=h(APPROVER))
    assert r.status_code == 200 and r.json()["policy"]["approval"]["by"] == "u-priya"
    body = client.get(f"/api/incidents/{iid}", headers=h(VIEWER)).json()
    assert body["report"]["status"] == "closed_verified"
    assert body["report"]["approvals"][0]["by"] == "u-priya"
    ev = client.get(f"/api/incidents/{iid}/events?after=0", headers=h(VIEWER)).json()
    assert ev and all(e["n"] > 0 for e in ev)


# 14. API authorization on every sensitive route
SENSITIVE = [
    ("get", "/api/me"), ("get", "/api/scenarios"), ("get", "/api/incidents"),
    ("post", "/api/incidents"), ("get", "/api/incidents/{iid}"), ("get", "/api/incidents/{iid}/events"),
    ("post", "/api/incidents/{iid}/run"), ("post", "/api/incidents/{iid}/cancel"),
    ("post", "/api/incidents/{iid}/actions/{aid}/approve"), ("post", "/api/incidents/{iid}/actions/{aid}/reject"),
]

\[email]("method,path", SENSITIVE)
def test_every_route_requires_authentication(client, method, path):
    iid = new_incident(client)
    url = path.format(iid=iid, aid=f"{iid}-a6")
    assert getattr(client, method)(url).status_code == 401
    assert getattr(client, method)(url, headers=h("forged-token")).status_code == 401
    assert getattr(client, method)(url, headers={"Authorization": "Basic abc"}).status_code == 401

\[email]("method,path", [p for p in SENSITIVE if "{iid}" in p[1]])
def test_other_org_cannot_see_or_touch_incident(client, method, path):
    iid = new_incident(client)
    url = path.format(iid=iid, aid=f"{iid}-a6")
    assert getattr(client, method)(url, headers=h(OTHER)).status_code == 404


def test_other_org_incident_list_is_empty(client):
    new_incident(client)
    assert client.get("/api/incidents", headers=h(OTHER)).json() == []
    assert len(client.get("/api/incidents", headers=h(VIEWER)).json()) == 1


def test_roles_enforced(client):
    assert client.post("/api/incidents", json={}, headers=h(VIEWER)).status_code == 403
    iid = new_incident(client)
    assert client.post(f"/api/incidents/{iid}/run", headers=h(VIEWER)).status_code == 403
    client.post(f"/api/incidents/{iid}/run", headers=h(ANALYST))
    aid = revoke_id(client, iid)
    assert client.post(f"/api/incidents/{iid}/actions/{aid}/approve", headers=h(ANALYST)).status_code == 403
    assert client.post(f"/api/incidents/{iid}/actions/{aid}/reject", headers=h(VIEWER)).status_code == 403
    rep = client.get(f"/api/incidents/{iid}", headers=h(ANALYST)).json()["report"]
    assert rep["status"] == "awaiting_approval" and not rep["approvals"]


# 6. tampered request identity rejected\[email]("field", ["owner", "org", "created_by", "approver", "principal"])
def test_identity_fields_in_body_rejected(client, field):
    r = client.post("/api/incidents", json={"scenario": "clean", field: "u-priya"}, headers=h(ANALYST))
    assert r.status_code == 422
    iid = new_incident(client)
    client.post(f"/api/incidents/{iid}/run", headers=h(ANALYST))
    aid = revoke_id(client, iid)
    r = client.post(f"/api/incidents/{iid}/actions/{aid}/approve", json={field: "u-priya"}, headers=h(ANALYST))
    assert r.status_code in (403, 422)
    r = client.post(f"/api/incidents/{iid}/actions/{aid}/approve", json={"approved_by": "u-priya"},
                    headers=h(APPROVER))
    assert r.status_code == 422                 # even an approver cannot name someone else


def test_created_by_comes_from_token(client):
    iid = new_incident(client, token=APPROVER)
    inc = client.get(f"/api/incidents/{iid}", headers=h(ANALYST)).json()["report"]["incident"]
    assert inc["created_by"] == "u-priya" and inc["org"] == "acme"


def test_validation_and_limits(client):
    assert client.post("/api/incidents", json={"scenario": "rm -rf"}, headers=h(ANALYST)).status_code == 422
    big = json.dumps({"scenario": "clean", "x": "a" * 20000})
    r = client.post("/api/incidents", content=big, headers={**h(ANALYST), "Content-Type": "application/json"})
    assert r.status_code == 413
    assert client.get("/api/incidents/../../etc", headers=h(ANALYST)).status_code == 404
    assert client.get("/api/incidents/inc-zzzz", headers=h(ANALYST)).status_code == 404
    iid = new_incident(client)
    assert client.post(f"/api/incidents/{iid}/actions/inc-00000000-a1/approve",
                       headers=h(APPROVER)).status_code == 404


def test_rate_limit(tmp_path):
    app = create_app(db_path=str(tmp_path / "r.db"), tokens=DEMO_TOKENS, step_delay=0, background=False,
                     rate_limit=3)
    with TestClient(app) as c:
        codes = [c.get("/api/me", headers=h(VIEWER)).status_code for _ in range(4)]
    assert codes == [200, 200, 200, 429]


def test_errors_do_not_leak_internals(client, monkeypatch):
    from rook import engine
    monkeypatch.setattr(engine.Engine, "report", lambda *a, **k: 1 / 0)
    iid = new_incident(client)
    r = client.get(f"/api/incidents/{iid}", headers=h(ANALYST))
    assert r.status_code == 500 and r.json() == {"detail": "internal error"}


def test_double_run_and_closed_incident_conflicts(client):
    iid = new_incident(client, scenario="clean")
    client.post(f"/api/incidents/{iid}/run", headers=h(ANALYST))
    client.post(f"/api/incidents/{iid}/actions/{revoke_id(client, iid)}/approve", headers=h(APPROVER))
    assert client.post(f"/api/incidents/{iid}/run", headers=h(ANALYST)).status_code == 409
    r = client.post(f"/api/incidents/{iid}/actions/{revoke_id(client, iid)}/approve", headers=h(APPROVER))
    assert r.status_code == 409


def test_no_secrets_in_api_responses(client):
    iid = new_incident(client)
    client.post(f"/api/incidents/{iid}/run", headers=h(ANALYST))
    client.post(f"/api/incidents/{iid}/actions/{revoke_id(client, iid)}/approve", headers=h(APPROVER))
    body = client.get(f"/api/incidents/{iid}", headers=h(ANALYST)).text
    assert "sk_test_SYNTH" not in body and "closed_verified" in body

input.content:
# Keywarden

**Rook investigates, contains and verifies.**

Keywarden is a security incident-response product built around one agent, **Rook**. Rook doesn't stop at recommending a fix. It investigates a credential incident, takes authorized actions in a safe order, recovers from failed actions and checks the result independently. It closes the incident only when evidence shows every closure condition holds. We call this **Verified Closure**.

> Every integration in this repository is a **sandboxed mock** with synthetic credentials (`sk_test_SYNTH_*`). Keywarden is a hackathon build for neatHack 2026 and is not production-ready.

## The incident

A contractor, Jordan Doe, was offboarded and their directory account is disabled. Their payments API key is still active:

- they created it, and it is committed in `billing-api/.env.test`
- `billing-app` and `payments-worker` both authenticate with it, but the vault only records `billing-app`
- their cloud and project-tracker accounts were never disabled

Rook starts from the completed offboarding ticket and works through these steps:

1. **Investigate.** Rook reads the directory, accounts on three systems, vault metadata, live app and cloud config (it scans by fingerprint, so it finds the dependent that isn't recorded), and the commit history of the exposed file.
2. **Define closure first.** Rook writes 12 closure checks before it changes anything: the old key is rejected, the replacement works, nothing still uses the old key, and every dependent is configured, healthy and passing regression.
3. **Plan in a safe order.** The plan disables the leftover accounts, issues a replacement key, moves each dependent to it and only then revokes the old key. Code enforces this order whatever the planner proposes.
4. **Authorize.** Deterministic policy runs at plan time and again just before each action executes, against live state. Revocation can't be undone, so it waits for an approver from the incident's organisation.
5. **Execute, checkpoint and recover.** Each step persists to SQLite. When a tool call fails or times out, Rook inspects the real state before it decides whether a retry is safe. Retries reuse the same idempotency key.
6. **Verify independently.** Probes check authentication, health, regression suites and config fingerprints. A tool reporting success counts for nothing on its own.
7. **Close or escalate.** The incident closes only when every invariant holds. Otherwise it escalates with the exact unmet checks, and Rook never retries forever.

## Run it

Requirements: Python 3.10 to 3.13 and Node 18 or later.

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt

# 1. Terminal demo (no server). Signature scenario: a 503 mid-remediation, then recovery.
python -m rook.demo
python -m rook.demo --scenario persistent      # Rook escalates instead of claiming success

# 2. API + dashboard
uvicorn rook.api:create_app --factory --port 8000
cd web && npm install && npm run dev            # http://localhost:3000
```

In the dashboard, pick a scenario and click **Investigate offboarded contractor**, then **Run plan**. When Rook pauses, switch identity to **Priya (approver)** and approve the revocation. The run continues to closure. Switch to **Eve**, who belongs to a different company, and the incident disappears.

To trace to neatlogs, set `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` before starting the demo or the API. See [evidence/neatlogs-traces.md](evidence/neatlogs-traces.md).

### Tests and checks

```bash
python -m pytest -q                      # 58 tests
cd web && npx tsc --noEmit && npx next build
```

### Scenarios

`signature`, `clean`, `ambiguous_applied`, `ambiguous_lost`, `persistent`, `permission_denied`, `revoke_noop` (the vault says the key is revoked but it still works), `replacement_invalid`, `faulty_update`, `regression_fail`. They are listed in `rook/sandbox.py:SCENARIOS`. Failures are injected deterministically per operation.

## Architecture

```
web/ (Next.js)  ──/api proxy──▶  rook/api.py (FastAPI, bearer auth, org scoping)
                                     │
                                     ▼
                          rook/engine.py  Rook: investigate → conditions → plan → policy
                          │      │        → execute → reconcile → verify → close/escalate
             rook/policy.py  rook/verification.py (independent observers)
                          │
                rook/sandbox.py  five stateful mock adapters, idempotency, failure injection
                          │
                rook/store.py    SQLite: incidents, actions, conditions, checkpoints,
                                 tool_calls, approvals, run leases, append-only audit
                rook/obs.py      spans → neatlogs (OpenTelemetry), redacted
```

| Adapter | What it holds | Operations used |
|---|---|---|
| Source host | accounts, repos, commit audit log | find exposed key by fingerprint, commit history, disable account |
| Cloud | accounts, services with env vars | disable account, update service env |
| Internal app | identity directory, app config, health, regression | update config, health and regression probes |
| Project tracker | offboarding and security tickets | find completed offboardings, open, comment on and close tickets |
| Vault | versioned credentials | issue replacement, revoke version, authentication probe |

Key safety properties are listed in [evidence/security-notes.md](evidence/security-notes.md).

## Partner tools

- **neatlogs**: every workflow phase is a span (`incident.run` WORKFLOW, `investigate`/`plan` AGENT, `policy.*`/`verify`/`closure.evaluate` GUARDRAIL, `execute` TOOL, `reconcile`/`checkpoint.restore` CHAIN). Attributes cover incident ID, adapter, action type, attempt, decision and verification result. Secret values are never included. The before/after comparison is the remediation-order change. [Evidence](evidence/neatlogs-traces.md).
- **Entire**: checkpoints linking commits to the build sessions. [Evidence](evidence/entire-workflow.md).
- **cfo.ai**: the business plan behind Keywarden's pricing and costs. [Evidence](evidence/cfo-ai-business-plan.md).

## Limitations

- The adapters are in-process mocks. No real GitHub, cloud, vault or tracker is called.
- Demo bearer tokens are built in for local use. Set `KEYWARDEN_TOKENS` (JSON) and `KEYWARDEN_DEMO_TOKENS=0` anywhere shared.
- There is a single shared sandbox, so only one incident runs at a time.
- The optional model planner (`ROOK_PLANNER=llm`) only proposes actions. Ordering, policy and verification stay deterministic.

# Security notes

Keywarden is a sandbox: all five adapters are in-process mocks holding synthetic keys (`sk_test_SYNTH_*`). Nothing here is production-ready, and these notes describe what the build does and what it doesn't do.

## Agent safety

- **No arbitrary execution.** Rook can only perform four action types (`policy.ALLOWED`) against named services. There is no shell, network or file tool.
- **Least privilege and scope.** Every action must target a resource owned by the incident subject. If ownership can't be established, Rook blocks the action (fail closed, rule R2).
- **Safe order enforced in code.** `engine.enforce_order` adds issue → update → revoke edges whatever the planner (rule-based or model) proposes. Policy R4 blocks revocation while any live config still uses the old key. This is re-checked just before execution, so a dependent that appears late blocks it (`test_new_dependent_appearing_before_revocation_blocks_it`).
- **Human approval for irreversible steps.** Revocation needs an approver from the incident's org. The approver's identity comes from their authenticated principal and is stored in `approvals`.
- **Ambiguous outcomes.** Any timeout or transient error moves the action to `unknown`. Rook then probes real state before it decides between verified, safe retry and escalation. If it can't tell, it stops.
- **Bounded retries and steps.** `max_retries=3` and `max_steps=200`. Exhaustion leads to `failed` and escalation.
- **Verification is separate from execution.** Observers in `verification.py` never read adapter responses.
- **Append-only audit.** SQLite triggers reject `UPDATE`/`DELETE` on `audit`.

## API

- Bearer token on every route except `/api/health`. Tokens are looked up by SHA-256 digest with constant-time comparison, and the principal (id, org, roles) comes only from the token.
- Request bodies are strict (`extra="forbid"`). `owner`, `org`, `created_by`, `approver` and similar fields are rejected with 422.
- Object-level authorization: an incident from another org returns 404 on every route, so its existence isn't leaked either.
- Roles: `viewer` (read), `analyst` (create, run, cancel), `approver` (approve, reject).
- Limits: 8 KB request body (413), 60 requests/min per principal (429), strict id formats, scenario names from an enum.
- Errors: unhandled exceptions return `{"detail": "internal error"}` without a stack trace. Responses set `nosniff`, `no-store` and `no-referrer`.
- One executor per incident (SQLite lease). A second run gets 409.

## Secrets

- Stored audit events, checkpoints, tool outcomes and approvals go through `store.redact`, which replaces key values with `fp:` fingerprints.
- Trace attributes are redacted the same way. Keys matching `secret|token|password|authorization|api_key|value` are dropped before export (`test_secret_values_never_reach_trace_attributes`).
- The neatlogs API key is read from the environment and never logged or committed.

## Known limitations

- Demo tokens are built in for local runs. Disable them with `KEYWARDEN_DEMO_TOKENS=0` and set `KEYWARDEN_TOKENS`.
- There's no TLS termination, CSRF protection (bearer tokens only, no cookies) or token rotation.
- The sandbox is a single shared state, so one incident runs at a time.
- The rate limiter is in-memory and per process.
EOF

"""
PII masking support for Neatlogs spans.

Users supply a callable that receives the full span dict and returns
the (possibly modified) span dict. Returning None drops the span
entirely. The callable is responsible for traversing and redacting any
sensitive fields.

Example::

    def redact(span: dict) -> dict:
        attrs = span.get("attributes", {})
        for key in list(attrs):
            if "email" in key or "phone" in key:
                attrs[key] = "***"
        return span

    neatlogs.init(mask=redact)
"""

from typing import Any, Callable, Dict, Optional

# Module-level registry: str(id(fn)) -> callable
# Entries are permanent for the lifetime of the callable object; no cleanup needed.
_MASK_REGISTRY: Dict[str, Callable[[Dict[str, Any]], Optional[Dict[str, Any]]]] = {}


def register_mask(fn: Callable) -> str:
    """Register a mask callable and return its lookup key."""
    key = str(id(fn))
    _MASK_REGISTRY[key] = fn
    return key


def apply_mask(
    span_data: Dict[str, Any],
    global_mask: Optional[Callable],
) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """Apply the effective mask callable to *span_data*.

    Per-span mask (stored in ``attributes["neatlogs.mask_id"]``) takes
    precedence over the global mask.  Returns the (possibly modified) dict,
    or None when the mask dropped the span.
    """
    mask_id = (span_data.get("attributes") or {}).get("neatlogs.mask_id")
    mask_fn: Optional[Callable] = None

    if mask_id:
        mask_fn = _MASK_REGISTRY.get(str(mask_id))

    if mask_fn is None:
        mask_fn = global_mask

    if mask_fn is None:
        return span_data

    result = mask_fn(span_data)
    return result

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Deploy Keywarden (sandbox demo) to an AWS Lightsail container service.
#
# Needs: Docker, AWS CLI v2 with credentials for the account holding the hackathon credit,
# and the lightsailctl plugin (used by `aws lightsail push-container-image`).
# Optional: NEATLOGS_API_KEY in the environment, passed to the container so the live demo traces.
set -euo pipefail

SERVICE="${SERVICE:-keywarden}"
REGION="${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}"
POWER="${POWER:-nano}"          # smallest tier; plenty for a single-process demo
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

docker build -t keywarden:latest .

if ! aws lightsail get-container-services --service-name "$SERVICE" --region "$REGION" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  aws lightsail create-container-service --service-name "$SERVICE" --power "$POWER" --scale 1 --region "$REGION" >/dev/null
  echo "created container service $SERVICE ($POWER) in $REGION"
fi

state() { aws lightsail get-container-services --service-name "$SERVICE" --region "$REGION" \
            --query 'containerServices[0].state' --output text; }
until [[ "$(state)" == "READY" || "$(state)" == "RUNNING" ]]; do echo "waiting for service: $(state)"; sleep 15; done

aws lightsail push-container-image --service-name "$SERVICE" --label app --image keywarden:latest --region "$REGION"
IMAGE=$(aws lightsail get-container-images --service-name "$SERVICE" --region "$REGION" \
          --query 'containerImages[0].image' --output text)

TMP=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
python3 - "$IMAGE" > "$TMP/containers.json" <<'PY'
import json, os, sys
env = {"KEYWARDEN_STEP_DELAY": "0.6", "ROOK_VERSION": os.getenv("ROOK_VERSION", "aws")}
if os.getenv("NEATLOGS_API_KEY"):
    env["NEATLOGS_API_KEY"] = os.environ["NEATLOGS_API_KEY"]
print(json.dumps({"app": {"image": sys.argv[1], "ports": {"8000": "HTTP"}, "environment": env}}))
PY

{"containerName": "app", "containerPort": 8000,
 "healthCheck": {"path": "/api/health", "intervalSeconds": 10, "successCodes": "200"}}
JSON

aws lightsail create-container-service-deployment --service-name "$SERVICE" --region "$REGION" \
  --containers "file://$TMP/containers.json" --public-endpoint "file://$TMP/endpoint.json" >/dev/null

until [[ "$(state)" == "RUNNING" ]]; do echo "deploying: $(state)"; sleep 15; done

**Why AWS:** judges need a working demo link. The build environment also can't reach `ingest.neatlogs.com`, so a hosted instance with `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` set produces real neatlogs traces from real dashboard runs. Keywarden itself doesn't depend on AWS, and its adapters stay sandboxed mocks.

**Target:** one Lightsail container service (power `nano`, scale 1) runs the single image in `Dockerfile`, with the FastAPI backend and statically exported dashboard on port 8000. # Going live: neatlogs → AWS → Cloudflare

You end up with:

- **AWS Lightsail** running the Rook agent and API (one container, paid from the hackathon AWS credit)
- **Cloudflare Pages** serving the dashboard at a `*.pages.dev` address, forwarding `/api/*` to AWS
- **neatlogs** receiving a trace for every incident anyone runs on the live demo

Do the steps in order. Each one ends with a check, so you know it worked before moving on.

---

## 0. One-time tools on your computer

| Tool | Install | Check |
|---|---|---|
| Git + this repo | `git clone https://github.com/Timioni001/Rook && cd Rook && git checkout keywarden-build-v7m54f` | `ls rook` |
| Docker Desktop | https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/ (start it after installing) | `docker run --rm hello-world` |
| AWS CLI v2 | https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/getting-started-install.html | `aws --version` |
| Lightsail plugin | https://docs.aws.amazon.com/en_us/lightsail/latest/userguide/amazon-lightsail-install-software.html (`lightsailctl`) | `lightsailctl --version` |
| Node 18+ | https://nodejs.org | `node -v` |

---

## 1. neatlogs: get a project key and prove traces arrive

1. Sign in at https://app.neatlogs.com and create a project, for example `rook`.
2. Open the project settings, copy the **project API key**, and keep it private.
3. In a terminal in the repo:
   ```bash
   python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate      # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
   pip install -r requirements.txt
   export REDACTED                  # Windows PowerShell: $env:NEATLOGS_API_KEY="..."
   python -m neatlogs doctor --probe                        # SDK self-test against the real ingest
   python -m rook.demo                                      # one full incident, with a failure and recovery
   ```
4. **Check:** the demo prints `"status": "closed_verified"` and `"span_export_failures": 0`. In the neatlogs dashboard, under **Traces** or **Sessions**, a trace for workflow `rook-incident-response` appears within a few seconds. Open it and you'll see guardrail spans showing Passed/Blocked and tool spans for each adapter call.
5. **Before/after evidence**, for the submission:

   ```bash
   ROOK_DEMO_LABEL=before python -m rook.demo --scenario persistent
   git checkout keywarden-build-v7m54f
   ROOK_DEMO_LABEL=after python -m rook.demo --scenario signature
   ROOK_DEMO_LABEL=after python -m rook.demo --scenario persistent
   ```
   Copy the four trace URLs into `evidence/neatlogs-traces.md`. Each trace carries a `version:<commit>` tag, so you can filter before and after apart.
6. Optional dashboard setup, both in neatlogs: add a **Detection** with a regex on `sk_test_SYNTH`, which should never fire and acts as a leak tripwire. Add an **Alert** on `closure.evaluate` spans where `neatlogs.guardrail.passed = false`, which flags incidents that didn't close.

---

## 2. AWS: run the agent on Lightsail

1. In the AWS console, confirm the hackathon credit appears under **Billing → Credits**.
2. Create an access key for the CLI. The simplest route is **IAM → Users → (you) → Security credentials → Create access key → CLI**. Then:
   ```bash
   aws configure            # paste the key id + secret, region e.g. us-east-1, output json
   aws sts get-caller-identity
   ```
   **Check:** your account id is printed.
3. Deploy (the neatlogs key from step 1 is still exported in this terminal):
   ```bash
   export AWS_REGION=us-east-1
   ./deploy/aws-lightsail.sh
   ```
   The script builds the image, creates a `nano` container service called `rook`, pushes and deploys, then prints `Rook is live at: https://rook.xxxxx.us-east-1.cs.amazonlightsail.com/`. The first deploy takes a few minutes.
4. **Check:** open that URL. The Rook dashboard loads. Click **Investigate offboarded contractor**, then **Run plan**. A new session appears in neatlogs.
5. Look up the current price of the `nano` power in the Lightsail console before leaving it running. After judging, run `aws lightsail delete-container-service --service-name rook --region $AWS_REGION`.

## 3. Cloudflare: serve the dashboard on Pages

The dashboard is static files. A small Pages Function (`web/functions/api/[[path]].ts`) forwards `/api/*` to the AWS service, so the browser only ever talks to Cloudflare.

1. Create a free Cloudflare account at https://dash.cloudflare.com/sign-up.
2. Build and deploy from the `web` folder:
   ```bash

   ```
   The first run creates the `rook` Pages project and prints a `https://rook-xxx.pages.dev` URL.
3. Point the proxy at AWS: Cloudflare dashboard → **Workers & Pages → rook → Settings → Variables and Secrets → Add**, name `ROOK_API_ORIGIN`, value the Lightsail URL from step 2 without a trailing slash. Save, then redeploy (`npx wrangler pages deploy out --project-name rook`) so the function picks it up.
4. **Check:** `https://rook-xxx.pages.dev/api/health` returns `{"ok":true,...}`, and the dashboard runs an incident end to end. Use the `pages.dev` link as the demo link in the submission.
5. Optional: attach your own domain under **Custom domains** on the Pages project.

---

## Run everything locally instead

```bash

cd web && npm run dev                                   # terminal 2 → http://localhost:3000
# or the single container:
docker build -t rook . && docker run --rm -p 8000:8000 -e NEATLOGS_API_KEY rook   # http://localhost:8000
```

- The demo identities (analyst, approver, viewer, other company) are built into this sandbox build, so anyone with the link can use them. Writes are limited to 30 per minute per identity.
- Data lives on the container's disk and resets on every redeploy.
- Never commit `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` or AWS keys. Lightsail stores the neatlogs key in the container's settings only.

input.title: Rook: Verified Closure for the offboarded-contractor key incident
input.body:
Before: Rook rotated a leaked key by revoking it first and repairing the app afterwards. billing-app was down for several steps, and a persistent failure left it broken. The API had no authentication, and nothing was traced.

After: Rook investigates from the offboarding ticket and finds every service using the key, including one the vault doesn't record. It then issues a replacement, moves each service to it, and revokes the old key only after a person approves. Every failure is reconciled against real state before a retry, and a service that breaks on the new key is rolled back automatically. Once the leaked key is dead, Rook removes it from the repo. The incident closes only when 13 independently probed checks pass and the hash-chained audit log is intact; otherwise it escalates with explicit follow-ups. The API authenticates every route and scopes incidents per organisation. The agent emits neatlogs sessions with guardrail and tool spans. The dashboard can be served from Cloudflare Pages in front of the agent's AWS container.

How: five stateful sandbox adapters with deterministic failure injection (`rook/sandbox.py`); dependency-ordered planning, policy re-checked before each action, compensation, checkpoints and run leases (`rook/engine.py`, `rook/policy.py`, `rook/store.py`); observers that never read tool responses (`rook/verification.py`); a FastAPI factory with bearer auth and an evidence-pack export (`rook/api.py`); a Next.js dashboard with a Pages Function proxy (`web/`); a Dockerfile plus an AWS Lightsail script, with step-by-step setup in `deploy/README.md`. 69 tests pass. Measured before/after runs and the partner evidence status are in `evidence/`.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - Root ask from Timi: the "KEYWARDEN — MASTER BUILD INSTRUCTIONS FOR NEATHACK 2026". Build a real, testable incident-response agent called Rook with Verified Closure: five stateful mock adapters and a seeded incident (a contractor is disabled but their API key is still active, with dependents). Required: investigation, dependency graph, safe order, policy/authorization, approval, revoke/rotate, dependent updates, deterministic transient failure, checkpoint and reconciliation, independent verification, and an evidence-backed report. Also required: SQLite persistence, an API with server-side principal and object-level authz, neatlogs real traces with a before/after pair, Entire, reuse of the existing cfo.ai plan (no fabrication), a dashboard, 14 test scenarios, an evidence/ directory, and a demo script under 3 minutes. Report at each milestone with files changed, what works, commands run, blockers and next step.
   - Coordinator context: deadline Mon Oct 12 23:55 IST (18:25 UTC); scoring is agent 30, tools 25, video 20, build-in-public 15, originality 10.
   - Security/attribution rule (verbatim intent, from memory): "Commits/PRs to Timioni001/Rook must not leave Claude traces: no Co-Authored-By Claude, no Claude-Session lines, no Claude mentions in messages, PR bodies, or code." Never expose secret env values. Never ask the user to paste keys in chat. Use synthetic credentials only, no real production systems, no arbitrary shell execution, and don't fabricate evidence or financial numbers.
   - Later asks: use the AWS $25 credit, cfo.ai usage, and research and integrate neatlogs features. Skip Entire (chosen on the decision card). Restyle the UI like the reference image (white, black panels, lime highlights, simple). Latest ask: "give me steps on the aws and the neat logs also lets deploy to cloudflare and lets use the name as rook key warden is just side also we have to include more features that makes this agent have solution to traditional problems".

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Python 3.13, FastAPI (factory `uvicorn rook.api:create_app --factory`), Pydantic v2 (extra="forbid"), SQLite (append-only audit triggers plus a hash chain), pytest (69 passing).
   - Next.js 14 app router with TypeScript. Static export via STATIC_EXPORT=1 into web/out, served by the backend or by Cloudflare Pages with the Function web/functions/api/[[path]].ts proxying to ROOK_API_ORIGIN.
   - neatlogs SDK 1.4.26: init(api_key, workflow_name, tags, user_id, mask, capture_logs, pii_enabled, instrumentations, tracer_provider for tests); trace(name, kind, session_id, end_user_id, end_user_metadata, version); custom attributes neatlogs.guardrail.*, neatlogs.tool.*, neatlogs.retriever.*; neatlogs.log; get_delivery_diagnostics. The container blocks ingest.neatlogs.com.
   - Engine flow: investigate → closure conditions defined first → plan (issue → update dependents → revoke → scrub, enforced by enforce_order) → policy R0–R7 (re-checked before execution) → execute → reconcile on transient/timeout (unknown → applied probe → verified/retry/failed) → verify via independent observers → checkpoint → compensate (rollback) → finalize (close/escalate) plus a PM ticket.
   - Run lease table, idempotency keys, checkpoint_restored on restart, bounded retries (max 3, then 4 attempts gives failed).
   - Docker image uses public.ecr.aws base images. The build here failed with 429; it's untested in the container. AWS Lightsail nano container deploy script.

3. Files and Code Sections (all in /home/claude/Rook):
   - rook/domain.py: Status and TRANSITIONS (authorized→blocked, retry_pending→blocked added), IncidentStatus (investigating, ready, awaiting_approval, remediating, escalated, closed_verified, open), Incident (org, created_by, subject, title, severity, scenario, status, closed_at, relationships, graph, findings, exposure, ticket), Action (depends_on, summary, risk, idem_key, policy, result, evidence), Condition, Principal(id, org, roles, name, can()).
   - rook/sandbox.py: SCENARIOS (signature, clean, ambiguous_applied, ambiguous_lost, persistent, permission_denied, revoke_noop, replacement_invalid, faulty_update, regression_fail).
     - Seed: directory, github (jdoe disabled, billing-api/.env.test leaks OLD, audit_log), cloud (jdoe active, payments-worker env uses OLD, which is unrecorded in vault), pm (jdoe active, ghost ownerless, OPS-112 offboarding done), vault (cred-pay versions, used_by only app:billing-app), apps.
     - Adapters: SourceHost (find_secret, scrub_secret, commit_history), Cloud (set_secret_env), InternalApp, ProjectTracker (open_ticket/comment/set_status), Vault (issue_replacement, revoke, authenticate_fp, version_info, latest).
     - Sandbox: dependents_of_fp, dependent_config_fp, update_dependent, restore_dependent, ownerless_accounts, health, regression, mutate (idempotency plus failure injection), reset(scenario=).
   - rook/verification.py: observers account_disabled, old_credential_rejected, replacement_works, dependent_uses_replacement, dependent_healthy, regression_passes, no_dependents_on_old_key, secret_removed_from_repo; build_conditions (13 for the main incident); checks_for, verify_action, applied (reconciliation probe).
   - rook/policy.py: ALLOWED (disable_account, issue_replacement, update_dependent, revoke_credential, scrub_exposed_secret); NEEDS_APPROVAL={revoke_credential}; decide(a, inc, sb, plan, approval=None) returns (decision, reason, rule) for R1-allowlist, R2-ownership, R3-dependency, R4-safe-order, R5-approval and R0-default; may_compensate (R7).
   - rook/engine.py:
     - Module-level functions: investigate, build_graph, findings (including ownerless), RuleBasedPlanner (adds scrub after revoke), LLMPlanner (optional), enforce_order.
     - Engine: start(subject=None, org, created_by, scenario, extra_actions), approve(iid, aid, principal) (raises PermissionError when policy refuses), reject, run (lease) / _run (blocks needs_approval actions whose dependencies failed), _step, _exec, _compensate, report(iid, live=False), finalize.
     - Report helpers: follow_ups, evidence_pack(rep, audit, chain), blocked_reason, summarize, TOOL_DOCS.
     - Report contents: invariants (audit_chain_intact included); metrics tool_calls, failed_tool_calls (excludes rollback_ok), retries, checkpoints, audit_events, rollbacks, seconds_until_old_key_dead, seconds_until_closed.

I've renamed the product to Rook, added the Cloudflare deploy setup, written the AWS and neatlogs steps, and added five features for long-standing credential-incident problems. It's all pushed to PR #1. Nothing has actually been deployed yet: this container can't reach neatlogs or AWS, so those steps need to run on your computer. The 69 tests pass, and I checked the rollback scenario end to end in a browser.

**Your next step:** follow `go-live-steps.md` in order. Each section ends with a check so you know it worked.
1. **neatlogs:** copy your project key, then run `python -m neatlogs doctor --probe` and `python -m rook.demo`. The same section has the before/after commands for the trace evidence.
2. **AWS:** run `aws configure`, then `./deploy/aws-lightsail.sh`. It prints a Lightsail URL running Rook with your neatlogs key.
3. **Cloudflare:** run `npx wrangler pages deploy out --project-name rook`, then set `ROOK_API_ORIGIN` to the Lightsail URL in the Pages settings. Use the `pages.dev` link as your demo link.

**Name:** the product, dashboard, AWS service and Cloudflare project are all called Rook now. Keywarden only appears as the team name.

**New features:**
- **Rollback:** if an update breaks a service, Rook moves it back to the old key and holds off revoking that key. The screenshot shows this.
- **Repo cleanup:** after revoking, Rook removes the dead key from the file it leaked in. It flags the git history for a person to clean.
- **Ownerless accounts:** Rook flags accounts nobody owns for a person and never acts on them itself.
- **Tamper-evident audit log:** each entry is linked to the one before it, and a broken link blocks closing the incident. There's also a one-click evidence pack you can download.
- **Metrics:** Rook records how long the leaked key stayed live, time to close, retries, rollbacks and checkpoints.

- **Docker image never built:** the image registries rate-limited me here, so the AWS script will be its first real build.

"""Rook: a bounded, tool-using incident-response agent with Verified Closure.

INVESTIGATE -> DEFINE CLOSURE -> PLAN (dependency graph) -> AUTHORIZE -> EXECUTE -> VERIFY
-> CHECKPOINT -> RECOVER / ESCALATE -> CLOSE ONLY ON EVIDENCE.

All state lives in SQLite, so a run can stop at any point (crash, approval wait, cancel) and be
resumed by a new process from the last checkpoint.
"""
import json, os, time, uuid
from .domain import Action, Condition, Incident, IncidentStatus as IS, Status, fp
from .sandbox import Transient, Permanent, Timeout
from . import policy
from .verification import applied, build_conditions, evaluate, verify_action
from .obs import log, span

S = Status
RUNNABLE = {S.authorized, S.retry_pending, S.executing, S.executed, S.unknown}
UNRESOLVED_BAD = {S.failed, S.blocked, S.unknown}


TOOL_DOCS = {
    "disable_account": "Disable a user account on a connected service (sandbox)",
    "issue_replacement": "Create a new version of a credential in the vault; old version stays valid",
    "update_dependent": "Point an application or cloud service at the newest credential version",
    "revoke_credential": "Permanently revoke one credential version in the vault",
    "scrub_exposed_secret": "Replace a leaked key in a tracked file with a placeholder",
}


class SimulatedCrash(BaseException):      # BaseException so no handler swallows it
    ...


class RunInProgress(Exception):
    ...


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- investigation

def investigate(sb, subject):
    """Observed relationships, graph and findings. Fingerprints and paths only; no secret values."""
    rel = []
    person = sb.apps.directory(subject)
    for name in ("github", "cloud", "pm"):
        for u, acc in sb.account_service(name).accounts().items():
            if acc["owner"] == subject:
                rel.append({"rel": "has_account", "service": name, "user": u, "status": acc["status"]})
    for cid in sorted(sb.vault.creds()):
        m = sb.vault.meta(cid)
        if m["owner"] != subject:
            continue
        active = [v for v in m["versions"] if v["status"] == "active"]
        cur = active[-1] if active else m["versions"][-1]
        deps = sb.dependents_of_fp(cur["fp"])
        exposed = sb.github.find_secret(cur["fp"])
        rel.append({"rel": "owns_credential", "cred": cid, "status": "active" if active else "inactive",
                    "version": cur["v"], "fp": cur["fp"], "purpose": m["purpose"],
                    "created_by": m["created_by"], "created_at": m["created_at"],
                    "dependents": deps, "recorded_used_by": m["used_by"],
                    "unrecorded_dependents": [d for d in deps if d not in m["used_by"]],
                    "exposed_in": exposed,
                    "exposure_history": [h for p in exposed for h in sb.github.commit_history(p)]})
    for o in sb.ownerless_accounts():          # not this subject's, but found on the same sweep
        rel.append({"rel": "ownerless_account", **o})
    return person, rel, build_graph(subject, person, rel), findings(subject, person, rel)


def build_graph(subject, person, rel):
    nodes = [{"id": subject, "kind": "identity", "label": person.get("name", subject),
              "status": person.get("status", "unknown"), "detail": person.get("type", "")}]
    edges = []
    for r in rel:
        if r["rel"] == "has_account":
            nid = f"{r['service']}:{r['user']}"
            nodes.append({"id": nid, "kind": "account", "label": f"{r['service']} / {r['user']}", "status": r["status"]})
            edges.append({"from": subject, "to": nid, "rel": "has account"})
        elif r["rel"] == "owns_credential":
            nodes.append({"id": r["cred"], "kind": "credential", "label": f"{r['cred']} ({r['fp']})",
                          "status": r["status"], "detail": r["purpose"]})
            edges.append({"from": subject, "to": r["cred"], "rel": "created"})
            for d in r["dependents"]:
                nodes.append({"id": d, "kind": "dependent", "label": d, "status": "uses old key",
                              "detail": "not in vault metadata" if d in r["unrecorded_dependents"] else ""})
                edges.append({"from": d, "to": r["cred"], "rel": "authenticates with"})
            for p in r["exposed_in"]:
                nodes.append({"id": f"repo:{p}", "kind": "repo", "label": p, "status": "exposed"})
                edges.append({"from": r["cred"], "to": f"repo:{p}", "rel": "committed to"})
    return {"nodes": nodes, "edges": edges}


def findings(subject, person, rel):
    out = []
    name = person.get("name", subject)
    dis = [f"{r['service']}/{r['user']}" for r in rel if r["rel"] == "has_account" and r["status"] == "disabled"]
    act = [f"{r['service']}/{r['user']}" for r in rel if r["rel"] == "has_account" and r["status"] == "active"]
    out.append({"severity": "info", "text": f"{name} ({person.get('type', 'unknown type')}) is "
                f"{person.get('status', 'unknown')} in the directory since {person.get('disabled_at', 'n/a')}.",
                "evidence": {"directory_status": person.get("status")}})
    if act:
        out.append({"severity": "medium", "text": f"Accounts still active after offboarding: {', '.join(act)}. "
                    f"Already disabled: {', '.join(dis) or 'none'}.", "evidence": {"active": act, "disabled": dis}})
    for r in rel:
        if r["rel"] != "owns_credential" or r["status"] != "active":
            continue
        out.append({"severity": "high", "text": f"{r['purpose']} {r['cred']} ({r['fp']}) created by {r['created_by']} "
                    f"on {r['created_at'][:10]} is still active.", "evidence": {"cred": r["cred"], "version": r["version"]}})
        if r["dependents"]:
            out.append({"severity": "high", "text": f"It is in live use by {', '.join(r['dependents'])}; revoking it "
                        "first would take them down, so each must move to a replacement key before revocation.",
                        "evidence": {"dependents": r["dependents"]}})
        if r["unrecorded_dependents"]:
            out.append({"severity": "medium", "text": f"{', '.join(r['unrecorded_dependents'])} uses the key but is "
                        "missing from the vault's metadata; found by scanning live configuration.",
                        "evidence": {"recorded_used_by": r["recorded_used_by"]}})
        for h in r["exposure_history"]:
            out.append({"severity": "high", "text": f"The key is committed in {h['repo']}/{h['path']} "
                        f"(by {h['actor']} on {h['at'][:10]}), so it must be treated as leaked.", "evidence": h})
    for r in rel:
        if r["rel"] == "ownerless_account":
            out.append({"severity": "medium", "text": f"{r['service']} account '{r['user']}' has no owner in any "
                        "directory. Rook will not touch access it cannot attribute; a person needs to assign or "
                        "remove it.", "evidence": {"service": r["service"], "user": r["user"], "status": r["status"]}})
    return out


def explain(person, rel):
    return " ".join(f["text"] for f in findings(person.get("id", ""), person, rel)[1:]) if rel else ""


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- planning

def make_action(iid, n, type, target, params, depends_on=(), summary="", risk="low"):
    return Action(id=f"{iid}-a{n}", incident_id=iid, type=type, target=target, params=params,
                  depends_on=list(depends_on), summary=summary, risk=risk,
                  idem_key=f"{iid}:{type}:{params.get('service','')}:{target}")


class RuleBasedPlanner:
    """Deterministic plan: contain accounts, then replace -> repoint dependents -> revoke."""
    def plan(self, rel, iid):
        acts = []

        def add(t, target, deps=(), summary="", risk="low", **p):
            a = make_action(iid, len(acts) + 1, t, target, p, deps, summary, risk)
            acts.append(a)
            return a
        for r in rel:
            if r["rel"] == "has_account" and r["status"] == "active":
                add("disable_account", r["user"], service=r["service"],
                    summary=f"Disable the leftover {r['service']} account '{r['user']}'.")
        for r in rel:
            if r["rel"] != "owns_credential" or r["status"] != "active":
                continue
            c = r["cred"]
            issue = add("issue_replacement", c, service="vault", old_version=r["version"], old_fp=r["fp"],
                        summary=f"Create a new version of {c}. The old key keeps working for now.")
            ups = [add("update_dependent", d, [issue.id], service=d.split(":")[0], cred_id=c,
                       old_fp=r["fp"], old_version=r["version"],
                       summary=f"Point {d} at the new key and check it is healthy.") for d in r["dependents"]]
            rev = add("revoke_credential", c, [u.id for u in ups] + [issue.id], service="vault", cred_id=c,
                      version=r["version"], old_fp=r["fp"], risk="high",
                      summary=f"Permanently revoke the old key {r['fp']}. Anything still using it will stop working.")
            for path in r.get("exposed_in", []):
                add("scrub_exposed_secret", path, [rev.id], service="github", cred_id=c, old_fp=r["fp"],
                    summary=f"Remove the leaked (now dead) key from {path} so scanners stop flagging it.")
        return acts


class LLMPlanner:
    """Model proposes from fingerprint-only observations; ordering and policy are enforced in code."""
    def __init__(self):
        self.fallback = RuleBasedPlanner()

    def plan(self, rel, iid):
        try:
            import anthropic
            m = anthropic.Anthropic().messages.create(
                model=os.getenv("ROOK_MODEL", "[model]"), max_tokens=1500,
                system=("You plan credential incident remediation. Return ONLY a JSON list of "
                        "{type,target,params,summary}. Types: disable_account (params.service github|cloud|pm), "
                        "issue_replacement (target cred id, params.service='vault'), update_dependent (target "
                        "'app:x' or 'cloud:y', params.service app|cloud, params.cred_id), revoke_credential "
                        "(target cred id, params.service='vault'). Secrets are fingerprints."),
                messages=[{"role": "user", "content": json.dumps(rel)}])
            raw = json.loads(m.content[0].text)
            by_cred = {r["cred"]: r for r in rel if r["rel"] == "owns_credential"}
            acts = []
            for x in raw:
                if x.get("type") not in policy.ALLOWED:
                    continue
                p = dict(x.get("params", {}))
                cred = x["target"] if x["type"] in ("issue_replacement", "revoke_credential") else p.get("cred_id")
                if cred in by_cred:                         # observed truth overrides model input
                    p.update(old_fp=by_cred[cred]["fp"], old_version=by_cred[cred]["version"])
                    if x["type"] == "revoke_credential":
                        p.update(cred_id=cred, version=by_cred[cred]["version"])
                acts.append(make_action(iid, len(acts) + 1, x["type"], x["target"], p,
                                        summary=x.get("summary", ""),
                                        risk="high" if x["type"] in policy.NEEDS_APPROVAL else "low"))
            return acts or self.fallback.plan(rel, iid)
        except Exception:
            return self.fallback.plan(rel, iid)


def enforce_order(plan):
    """Add the dependency edges safety requires (whatever the planner said) and topologically sort.

    issue_replacement -> update_dependent(s) -> revoke_credential, per credential.
    """
    by_id = {a.id: a for a in plan}
    for a in plan:
        cred = a.target if a.type in ("issue_replacement", "revoke_credential") else a.params.get("cred_id")
        need = []
        if a.type == "update_dependent":
            need = [x.id for x in plan if x.type == "issue_replacement" and x.target == cred]
        if a.type == "revoke_credential":
            need = [x.id for x in plan if x.type in ("issue_replacement", "update_dependent")
                    and (x.target == cred or x.params.get("cred_id") == cred)]
        if a.type == "scrub_exposed_secret":             # only touch the file once the key is dead
            need = [x.id for x in plan if x.type == "revoke_credential" and x.target == cred]
        a.depends_on = sorted(set(d for d in a.depends_on if d in by_id) | set(need))
    order, seen, temp = [], set(), set()

    def visit(a):
        if a.id in seen:
            return
        if a.id in temp:
            raise ValueError("dependency cycle in plan")
        temp.add(a.id)
        for d in a.depends_on:
            visit(by_id[d])
        temp.discard(a.id)
        seen.add(a.id)
        order.append(a)
    for a in plan:
        visit(a)
    return order


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- engine

class Engine:
    def __init__(self, store, sb, planner=None, max_steps=200, max_retries=3,
                 sleep=time.sleep, crash_after=None, step_delay=0.0):
        self.store, self.sb = store, sb
        self.planner = planner or (LLMPlanner() if os.getenv("ROOK_PLANNER") == "llm" else RuleBasedPlanner())
        self.max_steps, self.max_retries = max_steps, max_retries
        self.sleep, self.crash_after, self.step_delay = sleep, crash_after, step_delay
        self.executions = 0
        self.cancelled = False

    def cancel(self):
        self.cancelled = True

    # ---- INVESTIGATE -> DEFINE CLOSURE -> PLAN -> AUTHORIZE ----
    def start(self, subject=None, org="acme", created_by="system", scenario=None, extra_actions=()):
        iid = "inc-" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]
        with span("incident.start", session=iid, user=created_by, user_meta={"org": org},
                  incident=iid, org=org, scenario=scenario or "") as root:
            if subject is None:                       # trigger: completed offboarding tickets
                done = self.sb.pm.completed_offboardings()
                subject = next(iter(done.values()))["subject"] if done else None
                if subject is None:
                    raise ValueError("no completed offboarding to investigate")
            with span("investigate", incident=iid) as sp:
                person, rel, graph, finds = investigate(self.sb, subject)
                sp.set(accounts=sum(r["rel"] == "has_account" for r in rel),
                       active_credentials=sum(r["rel"] == "owns_credential" and r["status"] == "active" for r in rel))
            with span("discover.dependencies", incident=iid) as sp:
                deps = [d for r in rel if r["rel"] == "owns_credential" for d in r["dependents"]]
                sp.retriever("config scan for " + ", ".join(r["fp"] for r in rel if r["rel"] == "owns_credential"),
                             deps)
                sp.set(dependents=len(deps), unrecorded=sum(len(r.get("unrecorded_dependents", [])) for r in rel
                                                            if r["rel"] == "owns_credential"))
            inc = Incident(id=iid, org=org, created_by=created_by, subject=subject, scenario=scenario or "custom",
                           title=f"Active credential after offboarding: {person.get('name', subject)}",
                           relationships=rel, graph=graph, findings=finds,
                           exposure=" ".join(f["text"] for f in finds),
                           severity="high" if any(f["severity"] == "high" for f in finds) else "medium")
            self.store.save_incident(inc)
            self.store.audit(iid, "investigated", {"relationships": rel, "findings": [f["text"] for f in finds]})

            conds = build_conditions(rel)                  # defined BEFORE any remediation
            self.store.save_conditions(iid, conds)
            self.store.audit(iid, "closure_conditions_defined", {"conditions": [c.id for c in conds]})

            try:
                inc.ticket = self.sb.pm.open_ticket(inc.title, subject, f"{iid}:ticket")["ticket"]
                self.store.audit(iid, "ticket_opened", {"ticket": inc.ticket})
            except (Transient, Timeout, Permanent) as e:   # tracking is best effort, never blocks containment
                self.store.audit(iid, "ticket_open_failed", {"error": type(e).__name__})

            with span("plan", incident=iid) as sp:
                plan = self.planner.plan(rel, iid) + list(extra_actions)
                plan = enforce_order(plan)
                sp.set(actions=len(plan), planner=type(self.planner).__name__)
            # stable ids in execution order; references rewritten accordingly
            rename = {a.id: f"{iid}-a{i+1}" for i, a in enumerate(plan)}
            seen = set()
            for i, a in enumerate(plan):
                a.id, a.incident_id = rename[a.id], iid
                a.depends_on = [rename[d] for d in a.depends_on]
                a.idem_key = f"{iid}:{a.type}:{a.params.get('service','')}:{a.target}"
                a.max_retries = self.max_retries
            for i, a in enumerate(plan):
                with span("policy.decide", incident=iid, action=a.id, action_type=a.type, target=a.target) as sp:
                    if a.idem_key in seen:
                        decision, reason, rule = "blocked", "Duplicate of another planned action.", "R6-duplicate"
                    else:
                        decision, reason, rule = policy.decide(a, inc, self.sb, plan)
                    sp.set(decision=decision, rule=rule)
                    sp.guardrail(f"{a.type} {a.target}", decision != "blocked", f"{decision} ({rule}): {reason}")
                seen.add(a.idem_key)
                a.policy = {"decision": decision, "reason": reason, "rule": rule}
                a.move({"authorized": S.authorized, "needs_approval": S.needs_approval}.get(decision, S.blocked))
                self.store.add_action(a, i)
                self.store.audit(iid, "policy_" + decision, {"action": a.id, "type": a.type, "target": a.target,
                                                             "reason": reason, "rule": rule})
                if decision == "blocked":
                    self.store.audit(iid, "escalated", {"action": a.id, "reason": reason})
            self.store.checkpoint(iid, "planned", {"statuses": {a.id: a.status.value for a in plan}})
            inc.status = IS.ready.value         # approval is asked for when the run reaches that step
            self.store.save_incident(inc)
            root.set(subject=subject, actions=len(plan), status=inc.status)
        return inc

    # ---- human approval (policy re-checked; approver identity comes from the caller's principal) ----
    def approve(self, iid, action_id, principal):
        a = self._action(iid, action_id)
        if a.status != S.needs_approval:
            raise ValueError(f"{action_id} is {a.status.value}, not awaiting approval")
        inc = self.store.incident(iid)
        approval = {"by": principal.id, "roles": list(principal.roles), "org": principal.org}
        with span("approval.decide", session=iid, user=principal.id, user_meta={"org": principal.org},
                  incident=iid, action=action_id, approver=principal.id) as sp:
            decision, reason, rule = policy.decide(a, inc, self.sb, self.store.actions(iid), approval=approval)
            sp.set(decision=decision)
            sp.guardrail(f"approve {a.type} {a.target} by {principal.id}", decision == "authorized", reason)
        if decision == "authorized":
            a.move(S.authorized)
            a.policy = {"decision": "authorized", "reason": reason, "rule": rule, "approval": approval}
            self.store.approval(iid, a.id, "approved", principal.id, {"reason": reason})
            self.store.audit(iid, "approval_granted", {"action": a.id, "by": principal.id})
        else:
            self.store.approval(iid, a.id, "refused_by_policy", principal.id, {"reason": reason})
            self.store.audit(iid, "approval_rejected_by_policy", {"action": a.id, "by": principal.id, "reason": reason})
            raise PermissionError(reason)
        self.store.save_action(a)
        return a

    def reject(self, iid, action_id, principal, note=""):
        a = self._action(iid, action_id)
        if a.status != S.needs_approval:
            raise ValueError(f"{action_id} is {a.status.value}, not awaiting approval")
        a.move(S.blocked)
        a.policy = {**a.policy, "decision": "blocked", "reason": f"Rejected by {principal.id}. {note}".strip()}
        self.store.save_action(a)
        self.store.approval(iid, a.id, "rejected", principal.id, {"note": note[:500]})
        self.store.audit(iid, "approval_rejected", {"action": a.id, "by": principal.id})
        return a

    def _action(self, iid, action_id):
        a = next((x for x in self.store.actions(iid) if x.id == action_id), None)
        if a is None:
            raise KeyError(action_id)
        return a

    # ---- EXECUTE -> VERIFY -> CHECKPOINT -> CONTINUE OR RECOVER (resumable from the DB) ----
    def run(self, iid):
        owner = uuid.uuid4().hex
        if not self.store.acquire_run(iid, owner):
            raise RunInProgress(iid)
        try:
            return self._run(iid)
        finally:
            self.store.release_run(iid, owner)

    def _run(self, iid):
        steps = 0
        inc = self.store.incident(iid)
        with span("incident.run", session=iid, user=inc.created_by, user_meta={"org": inc.org},
                  incident=iid) as root:
            acts = self.store.actions(iid)
            inflight = [a.id for a in acts if a.status in (S.executing, S.executed, S.unknown)]
            if inflight:
                cp = self.store.last_checkpoint(iid)
                with span("checkpoint.restore", incident=iid, checkpoint=cp["n"] if cp else 0,
                          inflight=len(inflight)):
                    log("resuming from checkpoint {checkpoint}", checkpoint=cp["n"] if cp else None,
                        in_flight=",".join(inflight))
                    self.store.audit(iid, "checkpoint_restored", {"checkpoint": cp["n"] if cp else None,
                                                                  "label": cp["label"] if cp else None,
                                                                  "in_flight": inflight})
            inc.status = IS.remediating.value
            self.store.save_incident(inc)
            while steps < self.max_steps and not self.cancelled:
                acts = self.store.actions(iid)
                by_id = {a.id: a for a in acts}
                before = {a.id: (a.status, a.retries) for a in acts}
                for a in acts:
                    if self.cancelled or steps >= self.max_steps:
                        break
                    if a.status not in RUNNABLE and a.status != S.needs_approval:
                        continue
                    deps = [by_id[d] for d in a.depends_on]
                    bad = [d for d in deps if d.status in UNRESOLVED_BAD]
                    if a.status == S.needs_approval and not bad:
                        continue                          # waits for a person
                    if bad and a.status in (S.authorized, S.retry_pending, S.needs_approval):
                        a.move(S.blocked)
                        a.policy = {**a.policy, "decision": "blocked", "rule": "R4-safe-order",
                                    "reason": "Not run because " + ", ".join(f"{d.id} ({d.type}) is {d.status.value}"
                                                                             for d in bad) + "."}
                        self.store.save_action(a)
                        self.store.audit(iid, "blocked_by_dependency", {"action": a.id, "waiting_on": [d.id for d in bad]})
                        continue
                    if not all(d.status == S.verified for d in deps):
                        continue                          # waiting (e.g. on approval or a sibling step)
                    while a.status in RUNNABLE and steps < self.max_steps and not self.cancelled:
                        steps += 1
                        halt = self._step(a)
                        self.store.save_action(a)
                        self.store.checkpoint(iid, "step", {"step": steps, "action": a.id, "status": a.status.value,
                                                            "statuses": {x.id: (a if x.id == a.id else x).status.value
                                                                         for x in acts}})
                        by_id[a.id] = a
                        if self.step_delay:
                            time.sleep(self.step_delay)
                        if halt:
                            break
                after = {a.id: (a.status, a.retries) for a in self.store.actions(iid)}
                if after == before:
                    break
            for a in self.store.actions(iid):
                if a.status in (S.failed, S.unknown):
                    self.store.audit(iid, "escalated", {"action": a.id, "status": a.status.value,
                                                        "reason": a.result.get("error", "outcome could not be established")})
            if self.cancelled:
                self.store.audit(iid, "cancelled", {})
            rep = self.finalize(iid)
            root.set(status=rep["status"], steps=steps)
            return rep

    def _step(self, a):
        iid = a.incident_id
        attempt = a.retries + 1
        if a.status in (S.executing, S.unknown):
            # outcome uncertain: inspect real state BEFORE any new mutation
            with span("reconcile", incident=iid, action=a.id, action_type=a.type, attempt=a.retries) as sp:
                landed = applied(self.sb, a)
                sp.set(applied=landed)
                log("inspected live state for {action}: applied={applied}", action=a.id, applied=str(landed))
            if landed is True:
                ok, ev = verify_action(self.sb, a)
                a.evidence = ev
                if ok is True:
                    a.move(S.verified)
                    self.store.audit(iid, "reconciled_verified", {"action": a.id, "evidence": ev})
                elif ok is False:
                    a.move(S.failed)
                    a.result = {**a.result, "error": "Change landed but independent verification failed."}
                    self.store.audit(iid, "reconciled_but_verification_failed", {"action": a.id, "evidence": ev})
                    if a.type == "update_dependent":
                        self._compensate(a)
                else:
                    a.move(S.unknown)
                    self.store.audit(iid, "reconcile_inconclusive", {"action": a.id, "evidence": ev})
                    return True
            elif landed is False:
                if a.retries > a.max_retries:
                    a.move(S.failed)
                    a.result = {**a.result, "error": f"Gave up after {a.retries} failed attempts."}
                    self.store.audit(iid, "failed_retries_exhausted", {"action": a.id, "attempts": a.retries})
                else:
                    a.move(S.retry_pending)
                    self.store.audit(iid, "reconciled_not_applied", {"action": a.id, "safe_to_retry": True})
            else:
                a.move(S.unknown)
                self.store.audit(iid, "reconcile_inconclusive", {"action": a.id})
                return True

                decision, reason, rule = policy.decide(a, inc, self.sb, self.store.actions(iid),
                                                       approval=a.policy.get("approval"))
                sp.set(decision=decision, rule=rule)
                sp.guardrail(f"pre-execution check {a.type} {a.target}", decision == "authorized", reason)
            if decision != "authorized":
                a.move(S.blocked)
                a.policy = {**a.policy, "decision": "blocked", "reason": reason, "rule": rule}
                self.store.audit(iid, "policy_recheck_blocked", {"action": a.id, "reason": reason})
                return True

            self.store.save_action(a)
            self.store.audit(iid, "executing", {"action": a.id, "attempt": attempt})
            try:

138	class RuleBasedPlanner:
139	    """Deterministic plan: contain accounts, then replace -> repoint dependents -> revoke."""
140	    def plan(self, rel, iid):
141	        acts = []
142	
143	        def add(t, target, deps=(), summary="", risk="low", **p):
144	            a = make_action(iid, len(acts) + 1, t, target, p, deps, summary, risk)
145	            acts.append(a)
146	            return a
147	        for r in rel:
148	            if r["rel"] == "has_account" and r["status"] == "active":
149	                add("disable_account", r["user"], service=r["service"],
150	                    summary=f"Disable the leftover {r['service']} account '{r['user']}'.")
151	        for r in rel:
152	            if r["rel"] != "owns_credential" or r["status"] != "active":
153	                continue
154	            c = r["cred"]
155	            issue = add("issue_replacement", c, service="vault", old_version=r["version"], old_fp=r["fp"],
156	                        summary=f"Create a new version of {c}. The old key keeps working for now.")
157	            ups = [add("update_dependent", d, [issue.id], service=d.split(":")[0], cred_id=c,
158	                       old_fp=r["fp"], old_version=r["version"],
159	                       summary=f"Point {d} at the new key and check it is healthy.") for d in r["dependents"]]
160	            rev = add("revoke_credential", c, [u.id for u in ups] + [issue.id], service="vault", cred_id=c,
161	                      version=r["version"], old_fp=r["fp"], risk="high",
162	                      summary=f"Permanently revoke the old key {r['fp']}. Anything still using it will stop working.")
163	            for path in r.get("exposed_in", []):
164	                add("scrub_exposed_secret", path, [rev.id], service="github", cred_id=c, old_fp=r["fp"],
165	                    summary=f"Remove the leaked (now dead) key from {path} so scanners stop flagging it.")
166	        return acts

169	class LLMPlanner:
170	    """Model proposes from fingerprint-only observations; ordering and policy are enforced in code."""
171	    def __init__(self):
172	        self.fallback = RuleBasedPlanner()
173	
174	    def plan(self, rel, iid):
175	        try:
176	            import anthropic
177	            m = anthropic.Anthropic().messages.create(
178	                model=os.getenv("ROOK_MODEL", "[model]"), max_tokens=1500,
179	                system=("You plan credential incident remediation. Return ONLY a JSON list of "
180	                        "{type,target,params,summary}. Types: disable_account (params.service github|cloud|pm), "
181	                        "issue_replacement (target cred id, params.service='vault'), update_dependent (target "
182	                        "'app:x' or 'cloud:y', params.service app|cloud, params.cred_id), revoke_credential "
183	                        "(target cred id, params.service='vault'). Secrets are fingerprints."),
184	                messages=[{"role": "user", "content": json.dumps(rel)}])
185	            raw = json.loads(m.content[0].text)
186	            by_cred = {r["cred"]: r for r in rel if r["rel"] == "owns_credential"}
187	            acts = []
188	            for x in raw:
189	                if x.get("type") not in policy.ALLOWED:
190	                    continue
191	                p = dict(x.get("params", {}))
192	                cred = x["target"] if x["type"] in ("issue_replacement", "revoke_credential") else p.get("cred_id")
193	                if cred in by_cred:                         # observed truth overrides model input
194	                    p.update(old_fp=by_cred[cred]["fp"], old_version=by_cred[cred]["version"])
195	                    if x["type"] == "revoke_credential":
196	                        p.update(cred_id=cred, version=by_cred[cred]["version"])
197	                acts.append(make_action(iid, len(acts) + 1, x["type"], x["target"], p,
198	                                        summary=x.get("summary", ""),
199	                                        risk="high" if x["type"] in policy.NEEDS_APPROVAL else "low"))
200	            return acts or self.fallback.plan(rel, iid)
201	        except Exception:
202	            return self.fallback.plan(rel, iid)

205	def enforce_order(plan):
206	    """Add the dependency edges safety requires (whatever the planner said) and topologically sort.
207	
208	    issue_replacement -> update_dependent(s) -> revoke_credential, per credential.
209	    """
210	    by_id = {a.id: a for a in plan}
211	    for a in plan:
212	        cred = a.target if a.type in ("issue_replacement", "revoke_credential") else a.params.get("cred_id")
213	        need = []
214	        if a.type == "update_dependent":
215	            need = [x.id for x in plan if x.type == "issue_replacement" and x.target == cred]
216	        if a.type == "revoke_credential":
217	            need = [x.id for x in plan if x.type in ("issue_replacement", "update_dependent")
218	                    and (x.target == cred or x.params.get("cred_id") == cred)]
219	        if a.type == "scrub_exposed_secret":             # only touch the file once the key is dead
220	            need = [x.id for x in plan if x.type == "revoke_credential" and x.target == cred]
221	        a.depends_on = sorted(set(d for d in a.depends_on if d in by_id) | set(need))
222	    order, seen, temp = [], set(), set()
223	
224	    def visit(a):
225	        if a.id in seen:
226	            return
227	        if a.id in temp:
228	            raise ValueError("dependency cycle in plan")
229	        temp.add(a.id)
230	        for d in a.depends_on:
231	            visit(by_id[d])
232	        temp.discard(a.id)
233	        seen.add(a.id)
234	        order.append(a)
235	    for a in plan:
236	        visit(a)
237	    return order
